items.label: Grey Hair on the Gatepost
items.text: A rub of grey hair on the gatepost at a mule's height, and one hoofprint that lands wrong. Somebody backed a dray in here.

items.label: The Getaway
items.text: Wheel-ruts over the kerb, a cart with the tail-board up. They did not care who saw.

items.label: Marks on the Sill
items.text: The print of a hand on the whitewash. Faint, but there.

result.label: The Hand Read
result.text: Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court.

items.label: Blood on the Glass
items.text: They cut themselves going in, or out.

result.label: The Blood Read
result.text: A great deal of it. The barber-surgeon in the Abbey Close stitched a hand the same morning.

witnesses: the woman at the casement opposite

items.label: Blood on the Latch
items.text: A smear of blood on the shutter latch. Someone cut themselves getting in, or getting out.

items.label: What Was Taken
items.text: the strongbox and everything in it: chosen, not grabbed. Whoever it was knew what was worth carrying.

items.label: Disturbed Dust
items.text: Something heavy was moved lately. Lately enough to date it.

items.label: Marks at the coal-hatch
items.text: Scuffs and splinters where the coal-hatch was worked open. They knew which way it gave.

journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: Two drunks, a stolen goose and a lost dog. The dog was the most reasonable of them. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at van der Meer's Pawnshop. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the board: Magdalena Visscher. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Pattern
journal.text: You took the Council's letter because something in this city does not add up: too many small crimes that fit together too neatly. Nobody else sees it yet. The first case on the desk is a burglary. Start there.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at van der Meer's Pawnshop
journal.text: Glass everywhere at Joan Barker's. Someone went through the shop window, with a cobble during the storm, took the window display, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing a cart with the tail-board up.
